chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Umar ibn Aban Al-Kalbi, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon them) saying: 'There is no fruit upon the face of the earth that was more beloved to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) than the pomegranate, and by Allah, whenever he ate it, he loved that no one else should share it with him.'
ai.seo_question: What was the Prophet's favorite fruit and how did he behave when eating it?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Fadala ibn Ayub, underscores the Prophet’s (SAW) deep affection for pomegranates, a fruit frequently cited in Shia tradition as a symbol of paradise and divine bounty. The detail that he preferred to eat it alone highlights a nuanced aspect of his personal habits (sunan) rather than stinginess, reflecting the human dimension of the Prophet’s life. This preference is often linked to the pomegranate’s mention in the Quran as one of the fruits of Jannah, reinforcing its spiritual significance in Islamic culture.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Umar Bin Aban Al Kalby who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> both<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is no fruit upon the surface of the earth more beloved to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> than the Pomegranate, and, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup> whenever I<sup>asws</sup> have eat it I<sup>asws</sup> love it that no one else should participate in it with me’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from Fadalah ibn from ‘Umar ibn Aban al- Kalbiy who has said the following:

“I once heard abu Ja‘far, and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, saying, ‘No other fruit on earth was as much desirable to the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, as pomegranate. He (the Messenger of Allah) liked not to share it with anyone.’”
